subject.title: Feature: Activity-aware run timeout (wall-clock timeout kills active multi-tool runs)

question: Should OpenClaw replace the configured agent run timeout with an activity-aware idle timeout plus hard ceiling, or keep it as a wall-clock budget and only land narrower notice/channel/subagent fixes?
rationale: This changes core runtime semantics and probably config/default behavior, and the existing open PRs cover only slices of the requested product contract.

options.title: Adopt idle plus hard cap
options.body: Add an activity-aware idle deadline with an absolute maximum run budget and align timeout notices/tests around that canonical core contract.

options.title: Keep wall-clock semantics
options.body: Leave agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds as the hard run budget and limit follow-up work to clearer timeout messages, docs, and channel-specific progress.

options.title: Land slice fixes first
options.body: Treat the notification, subagent heartbeat, and Telegram progress PRs as separate improvements while deferring the umbrella timeout design.

recommendation.title: Adopt idle plus hard cap
recommendation.body: Add an activity-aware idle deadline with an absolute maximum run budget and align timeout notices/tests around that canonical core contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent timeout helper and gateway active-run history makes this the best available routing candidate for the core semantics decision.
